tests: an adapter requirement the spawn cannot meet refuses before a worktree, a branch, a task directory or a pool record exists

consumesExternalOutput.provenance: TWO OF THE FOUR POST-CONDITIONS THIS BEHAVIOR ASSERTS ARE NOT FILES. Criterion 2 requires that an unmet requirement leave the task directory, the pool record, `git worktree list` and `git branch --list` all unchanged, and the last two are another program's output. The capture at witness/captures/spawn-requirement-refusal-git-state.txt:1 was taken 2026-09-17 on node v26.6.0 in a scratch fleet built by the same helpers test/spawn.test.ts uses, printing both listings BEFORE any spawn and AFTER one successful spawn. HOW THIS WITNESS'S OWN NAMED TEST CONSUMES IT: the test reads both listings live before the refusal, asserts them byte-identical after it, and then runs a SUCCESSFUL spawn whose listings it checks against the captured contract (one line added to each, the worktree line ending in a bracketed task branch, the branch line marked `+` because it is checked out elsewhere). That control arm is what stops the unchanged-state assertions being satisfied by a kernel that creates nothing at all. The hook capture at witness/captures/spawn-turn-end-hook-record.txt:1 is cited because the same test drives that successful spawn to completion through the real generated turn-end hook, which src/spawn.ts runs with spawnSync, and asserts the record that child wrote against what the capture records. MEMBER 0 empties the derivation, so the check runs and finds nothing; MEMBER 1 leaves the derivation intact and downgrades the refusal to a warning, so the kernel knows and proceeds anyway. One is a blind check and the other is an ignored one, and both produce the same dangerous state by different routes.
